bib.title: Photorealistic Text-to-Image Diffusion Models with Deep Language Understanding

read.skipped: Appendix qualitative figure pages (A.1-A.4, A.17-A.30) are images; reference list skimmed

question: Can generic frozen text-only language models serve as text encoders for a cascaded text-to-image diffusion model, and how does that compare with scaling the image model?
hypothesis: Large frozen LMs pretrained on text only encode text for image synthesis better than image-text encoders, and scaling the text encoder helps more than scaling the U-Net (stated as a finding).
contributions: Frozen text-only LMs are very effective text encoders; scaling the text encoder improves quality more than scaling the diffusion U-Net
Dynamic thresholding for large classifier-free guidance weights
COCO zero-shot FID 7.27; human raters find Imagen on par with reference images for image-text alignment

method.summary: Imagen: a frozen T5-XXL encoder feeds a 64x64 text-conditional diffusion model, followed by two text-conditional super-resolution diffusion models (256, 1024), all with classifier-free guidance, dynamic thresholding and noise conditioning augmentation for the super-resolution models.

datasets.name: Internal image-text data
datasets.preprocessing: A subset filtered for pornographic imagery and toxic language

datasets.name: MS-COCO validation
datasets.size: 30K prompts for FID-30K; 200 caption-image pairs for human evaluation
datasets.preprocessing: Second human-eval set removes prompts containing person words (man, woman, people, child, etc.)

datasets.name: DrawBench
datasets.source: introduced here; includes prompts from DALL-E, Marcus et al., Reddit

models.name: Imagen base 64x64
models.architecture: U-Net adapted from Nichol & Dhariwal; text cross-attention at [32,16,8] plus attention-pooled text embedding; layer norm on text embeddings

models.name: Imagen SR 64->256
models.architecture: Efficient U-Net with self-attention and text cross-attention at lowest resolution

models.name: Imagen SR 256->1024
models.architecture: Efficient U-Net, no self-attention, text cross-attention kept; trained on 64->256 crops of 1024 images

other.ablated: BERT base/large, T5 small/base/large/XL/XXL, CLIP ViT-L/14 penultimate layer (all frozen)

training.objective: epsilon-prediction squared error, weighted denoising loss; classifier-free guidance by zeroing text embeddings with 10% probability; super-resolution models trained with noise conditioning augmentation, aug_level uniform in [0,1]
training.optimizer: Adafactor (base 64x64, default optax params); Adam b1=0.9 b2=0.999 eps=1e-8 (both super-resolution models)
training.lr_schedule: warmup_cosine_decay_schedule, peak 1e-4, decay_steps 2500000 (listing); cosine noise schedule for 64x64 and 64->256, 1000-step linear schedule (1e-4 to 0.02) for 256->1024
training.steps: 2.5M for all models (400K steps for the model-size ablation)
training.hardware: 256 TPU-v4 chips (base), 128 TPU-v4 chips (each super-resolution model)

inference.decoding: ancestral sampler; DDIM for certain models; classifier-free guidance with dynamic thresholding
inference.samples: Fair random samples, no post-processing or re-ranking; DrawBench uses 8 samples per model per prompt

metrics.name: FID-30K (zero-shot)
metrics.definition: 30K random COCO validation prompts, generated samples vs full validation reference images

metrics.name: Photorealism preference rate
metrics.definition: Percent of times raters pick model image over reference for 'Which image is more photorealistic (looks more real)?'

metrics.name: Caption alignment
metrics.definition: 'Does the caption accurately describe the above image?' yes/somewhat/no scored 100/50/0

metrics.name: DrawBench pairwise preference
metrics.definition: Raters compare 8-sample sets from models A and B on fidelity and alignment: prefer A, indifferent, prefer B

eval.protocol: COCO human eval: 200 image-caption pairs, batches of 50, interleaved control trials, only raters with at least 80% control accuracy kept, giving 73 (quality) and 51 (alignment) ratings per image. DrawBench: 25 raters per category (275 total), no rater filtering. 95% confidence intervals in Fig 3.

availability.data: DrawBench samples released (Appendix C); training data internal

prompts.text: Which set of images is of higher quality?
Which set of images better represents the text caption : {Text Caption}?
Which image is more photorealistic (looks more real)?
Does the caption accurately describe the above image?

evidence.quote: We use a batch size of 2048 and 2.5M training steps for all models.
we train a 2B parameter model for the 64 × 64 text-to-image synthesis, and 600M and 400M parameter models

results.claim: Imagen reaches zero-shot COCO FID-30K 7.27, ahead of DALL-E 2 (10.39) and GLIDE (12.24) and Make-A-Scene trained on COCO (7.55).
results.setup: MS-COCO 2014 validation, 256x256, 30K random prompts vs full validation reference images, zero-shot (no COCO training), guidance 1.35 for 64x64 model and 8.0 for super-resolution
results.quote: Imagen outperforms other methods on COCO [36] with zero-shot FID-30K of 7.27
results.note: Intro prints rounded 12.4, 10.4 and 7.6; Table 1 prints 12.24, 10.39, 7.55

results.claim: Raters prefer Imagen over real COCO images 39.5% of the time (text says 39.2%).
results.setup: 200 COCO validation pairs, 73 ratings per image; Imagen vs original, photorealism
results.note: Section 4.2 prints 39.2% and 43.6%; Table 2 prints 39.5 and 43.9 (no-people)

results.claim: On COCO prompts without people the photorealism preference rises to 43.9% (text: 43.6%).
results.setup: COCO subset with prompts containing person words removed
results.table: Table 2, row No people / Imagen, column Photorealism

results.claim: Caption alignment of Imagen is on par with original images (91.4 vs 91.9).
results.setup: COCO 200 pairs, 51 ratings per image, yes/somewhat/no scored 100/50/0

results.claim: Scaling the frozen text encoder improves quality more than scaling the U-Net.
results.setup: 64x64 model, CLIP vs FID-10K pareto curves over guidance weights; U-Net 300M to 2B, T5 small to XXL
results.quote: scaling the text encoder size to be signiﬁcantly more impactful than the U-Net size

results.claim: T5-XXL and CLIP encoders perform similarly on COCO but raters prefer T5-XXL on DrawBench in all 11 categories for alignment.
results.setup: 64x64 1B models with frozen T5-XXL vs CLIP; 300M models underperformed on DrawBench so 1B used
results.quote: human raters prefer T5-XXL over CLIP on DrawBench across all 11 categories
results.where: Sec 4.4, App D.1, Fig A.5b, A.7

results.claim: Dynamic thresholding gives better CLIP and comparable or better FID than static thresholding, especially at large guidance weights.
results.quote: dynamic thresholding results in samples with signiﬁcantly better photorealism and alignment with text

results.claim: Cross-attention over the text embedding sequence beats mean or attention pooling.
results.quote: conditioning over the sequence of text embeddings with cross attention signiﬁcantly outperforms simple mean or attention based pooling

results.claim: Efficient U-Net is 2-3x faster at sampling and converges faster than the standard U-Net.
results.setup: 64->256 super-resolution, FID-2K vs TPU training days (Fig A.14)
results.quote: Our Efﬁcient U-Net is also ×2 −3 faster at sampling.

results.claim: Noise conditioning augmentation is critical for super-resolution quality.
results.setup: 64->256 model, FID-10K, guidance sweep [1..18]; best samples use aug_level in [0.1, 0.3]
results.quote: Training with no noise augmentation generally results in worse CLIP and FID scores

results.claim: DrawBench: raters prefer Imagen over DALL-E 2 in 7 of 11 categories for alignment and all 11 for fidelity.
results.setup: DrawBench 200 prompts, 25 raters per category, 8 samples per set
results.quote: they prefer Imagen over DALL-E 2 in all 11 categories

results.claim: Imagen beats GLIDE on 8 of 11 categories for alignment and 10 of 11 for fidelity.
results.quote: Imagen outperforms GLIDE on 8 out of 11 categories on image-text alignment, and 10 out of 11 categories on image ﬁdelity.

results.claim: Human evaluation shows Imagen weaker on images of people, and internal checks found bias toward lighter skin tones and Western gender stereotypes for professions.
results.setup: Small-scale internal assessments; basis for not releasing code or demo
results.quote: an overall bias towards generating images of people with lighter skin tones and a tendency for images portraying different professions to align with Western gender stereotypes

limits: Code, weights and demo withheld because of bias, people-generation weakness and LAION-400M content audit
Weaker photorealism on images of people (39.5% vs 43.9% without people)
FID not fully aligned with perceptual quality, CLIP ineffective at counting
Bias analysis is preliminary and small scale
Ablations run on smaller 300M-2B base models with FID-10K, not the final configuration
DrawBench is only 200 prompts and no rater filtering; no seeds or significance tests besides 95% CIs
No total compute or wall-clock reported; sampling steps not stated

terms.definition: At each sampling step set s to a certain percentile absolute pixel value in the x-prediction; if s > 1, threshold to [-s, s] and divide by s
Corrupt the low-resolution conditioning image with noise at aug_level and condition the model on aug_level; random in training, swept at inference
